A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same arithmetic-diagnostic study. The core experiments, figures, and appendix results can be matched despite the revised title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical and symbolic addition evaluations, commutativity tests, prompting experiments, and fine-tuning results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds arithmetic-operation comparisons, commutativity controls, and contextual, mapping, and prompting experiments.

M1.justification: The core diagnostic framework remains numerical/symbolic addition, operand reversal, and digit-length testing, with the same principal prompting and SFT/DPO/RPO interventions. The additional mapping and reasoning variants are supplementary experimental controls; no redesigned core algorithm or model is established.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond addition to numerical and symbolic subtraction and multiplication (Table 3). It also tests addition embedded in natural-language templates and digit-to-digit shift-cipher representations (Appendices A.4-A.5), substantially broadening task and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-7B-Base as a comparator to instruction-tuned models (Table 8). The commutativity comparison also changes membership: new Llama/Qwen entries replace Gemma and Qwen2.5-14B entries from v1 Table 3. The broad addition-model comparison remains available in the matched appendix tables.

E3.justification: The commutativity evaluation adds temperature 0.0 and a 5-of-10 threshold alongside the previous temperature-0.7, 10-of-10 test. v2 also revises Phase 2 sampling from operands in [2^7, 2^49] to 3-20-digit pairs and states broader test-split restrictions for proprietary, reasoning, and fine-tuned models. Table 5 adds an undefined Map Acc. metric. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands robustness and failure analysis: temperature and consistency-threshold controls, natural-language contexts, base versus instruction-tuned models, conflicting shift-cipher mappings, and explicit intermediate-sum prompting (Table 1; Appendices A.4-A.5). These investigate alternative explanations absent from v1, alongside the retained prompting and fine-tuning analyses.

E5.justification: The numerical ± quantities accompanying accuracies in v1 Table 1 disappear from v2. Appendix A.2 retains ten evaluations for most models and single-evaluation exceptions. No increased repetition count or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for commutativity controls, other operations, Map Acc., and appendix experiments. For example, Table 3 reports Qwen2.5-7B-it multiplication accuracy of 17.29% numerically and 0.04% symbolically. All 44 rows of the complete addition-results table retain their numerical values (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 11). Some intervention results, including Llama2, Gemma2, and ERNIE rows in Table 4, are removed.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a probabilistic formulation using learned and ideal answer distributions, including approximate equality of answer distributions under operand reversal (Sections 3.1-3.2). v1 instead explicitly presented positional-addition and carry-propagation equations. This is a limited formalization change; neither version supplies theorems or proofs establishing the diagnostics.

C1.justification: The central pattern-matching-versus-rule-learning claim remains. v2 extends its conclusion to preliminary failures on other arithmetic operations, which v1 treated as future work. The abstract also replaces the claimed 81.2% average degradation from explicit rules with 29.49%, changing a prominent quantitative claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific hypotheses about model-family differences arising from training patterns, interprets instruction tuning as necessary for in-context learning, and argues that intermediate-state tracking does not explain the failures. It newly acknowledges unidentified circuit-level mechanisms and sampling limitations. The overarching pattern-matching interpretation and concerns about synthetic-task validity already existed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository address for the dataset and generation code and newly specifies ten independent symbolic mappings. Fine-tuning settings, hardware, and runtime remain documented in the relocated appendix. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit digit-length definitions for the three few-shot settings and shortens dated Gemini identifiers, reducing some implementation specificity.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to out-of-distribution generalization, reasoning-complexity studies, classic arithmetic benchmarks, and procedural versus associative reasoning, citing works such as Yuan, Roussinov, Shojaee, Saxton, and Berglund. Several model-report citations and the NTKEval discussion disappear. The central positioning as an elementary diagnostic complement to complex benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The title and most main-text sections are extensively rewritten. v2 organizes the narrative around three diagnostic properties, adds a Background and Motivation subsection, removes the standalone Discussion while redistributing its arguments, and reorganizes the appendices. This substantially changes the exposition beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned with an additional competition-mathematics example. The main accuracy tables are consolidated, the commutativity table gains temperature/threshold columns, Table 5 gains Map Acc., and several displays are condensed. New operation and appendix tables substantially expand the visual presentation; the complete addition table is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added operation, contextual, and diagnostic-control experiments address v1's narrow validation, while the access information and reorganized explanation improve scrutiny. The net gain is limited: core addition results remain unchanged, uncertainty values are removed, and new experimental details are incomplete. v2 also retains the abstract's claim of symbolic accuracy at most 7.5% despite Table 11 reporting 55.99% for Gemini 2.5 Pro.
